**Yes, but only some models, and it's not a guaranteed substitute for a real UPS.**

**What to look for**
- The maker must document UPS or EPS behavior with automatic switchover. A basic power station can drop out during an outage and reboot your PC ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- Look for a switchover time of 10-20 ms. EcoFlow warns that many stations advertised as UPS-capable switch over in 30 ms or more, which can risk data corruption, and says "9 times out of 10" the answer is no ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)).
- 10-20 ms is fast but not 0 ms. If your computer's manual requires 0 ms transfer, or you need an online double-conversion UPS, a dedicated UPS is the safer choice ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)).
- Confirm that charging from the wall while powering your computer (pass-through) is supported.
- Check your PC's power supply specs and the station maker's guidance before relying on it.

**Models with a listed switchover time** (from [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/portable-power-station-ups-transfer-time-computer-manufacturer-guidance-ecoflow-)):

| Model | Switchover | Capacity / output | Price (with code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2) | ≤10 ms | 288 Wh / 600 W | $275.50 (AFF5OFF) |
| [ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh) | ≤10 ms* | 1,024 Wh / 1,800 W | $395.10 (ALLPOWERS26) |
| [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) | ≤15 ms | 2,073.6 Wh / 2,600 W | $854.05 (AFF5OFF) |
| [BLUETTI Elite 300](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-300) | 10 ms | 3,014.4 Wh / 2,400 W | $1,199 (no working code; on pre-order at verification) |
| [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) | 20 ms | 1,152 Wh / 1,800 W | $474.05 (AFF5OFF) |

*The P1800's product images say 15 ms, and its store page contradicts itself on some specs.

**My picks**
- **Laptop or a small setup:** the Elite 30 V2 is the cheapest option with a 10 ms rating. Its 288 Wh is small, roughly four laptop charges.
- **Desktop plus router or monitors:** the ALLPOWERS P1800 offers the most capacity per dollar at 10 ms, but verify its specs given the conflicting listings.
- **Long outages:** the Elite 200 V2 or Elite 300 give much more runtime, but weigh about 24-26 kg.
- Prefer the 10 ms models over the 20 ms AC180 if your computer is sensitive to power gaps.

**Gaps in what I found:** The Dealectric records have no EcoFlow or Anker models, so I can't compare them. The EcoFlow and Anker pages I saw don't state a specific model's switchover time in the excerpts, so check the spec page for any model you're considering. The coupon prices were last tested Oct 21-24, 2026, so they may have changed.

The buy links are Dealectric affiliate links, so they earn a commission at no cost to you.

If you tell me your computer's wattage (or its power supply rating) and how long you want it to run in an outage, I can narrow this to one model.
